summary: Trinity County lookout: ground cabin built 1916, replaced 1937; seasonal staff 1931-1960; ruins remain at the summit per a hiking guide.

facts.design: White frame lookout house about 20 ft square at the base, with a 3-ft catwalk and windows (1954 survey); 1937 replacement was a Plan R1 cabin
facts.status_note: The lookout is no longer standing. A hiking guide says ruins of an old Forest Service lookout remain at the summit; the register gives no removal date.

staffing.status: seasonal lookouts named in newspaper clippings, 1931-1960; no later staffing found

access.note: A hiking guide describes a maintained trail to the summit, easily reached off Highway 3, and says overnight stays on the summit are still possible.

visit.trail_note: 8.4-mile trail to the summit, reached off Highway 3 (hiking guide)

facts.agency: Shasta-Trinity National Forest (administrator, per the register); Trinity National Forest (cooperator, per the register)

events.note: Original ground cabin built to a Region 5 1914 plan

Jack DeCordy served as lookout for a few weeks (November 1943 item)
Coast and Geodetic Survey station described on the lookout house; 16 ft tall, Forest Service property
Leroy Eisele scheduled to be lookout (May 1956 item)
Lookout brought out by pack train on October 10 (November 1960 item)

corrections.proposed: 1916 (original ground cabin); replaced 1937 with a Plan R1 cabin
corrections.why: The register says the original cabin was constructed in 1916 and was replaced in 1937; the brief records only the replacement year.
The register gives the removal date as unknown, and a hiking guide describes ruins of the old lookout at the summit.

notes_for_editor: Ruins at the summit rest on one hiking guide; the search summary claiming remnants was not used because the guide text itself is the source. Removal date is unknown per the register. The register lists Shasta-Trinity National Forest as administrator and Trinity National Forest as cooperator. It also gives a registration date of January 26, 2020, which the story does not use. The story rewords the 1932 and 1960 items and the hiking guide's ruins line; the guide gives no detail about the ruins. 1954 survey description and 1931-1960 clippings come from the Forest Lookouts page, which quotes them.
